names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 21 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Παχώμιος ο Νέος ο Οσιομάρτυρας», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 21. мај ст. ст., „Преподобни мученик Пахомије.“ — Преподобни мученик is the `venerable-martyr` this corpus puts in `types`; strip it and the bare forename is left, and the body repeats it bare once. **Uşaki, the Holy Mountain and Patmos are all in the body and none of them is part of the name**, and «Пахомије Усачки» is nowhere on the page. Measured before drafting with `foldchk.py`: `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` — **which is worth saying, because on 15 May this wave gave `pachomius-the-great` the form «Пахомије Велики» and not a bare «Пахомије» precisely because the Prologue printed Велики in that heading. The two readings together keep the corpus’s eleven other Pachomii out of a fold they would otherwise have joined.**

death.note: saint.gr: «ο Οσιομάρτυς Παχώμιος μαρτύρησε δι' αποκεφαλισμού το 1730 μ.Χ., την Πέμπτη της Αναλήψεως», and the head line «(; - 1730)».

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 21ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Παχώμιος ο Νέος ο Οσιομάρτυρας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 21 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing — and the page says he died «την Πέμπτη της Αναλήψεως», the Thursday of the Ascension, which is a paschal reckoning and not 21 Μαΐου in most years. The fixed day is the day the calendar keeps him on and is what the row records; the moveable day is the day he died. None of the corpus's Pachomii is this man: `pachomius-the-great` is the Egyptian, `pachomius-of-chios` and the others are of other places, and the two 05-15 Pachomii another reader drafted are Russians. Relics, as the page lists them: the monastery of Saint John the Theologian on Patmos, the skete of Kausokalyvia and the monasteries of Saint Paul and Nea Thebais on Athos, and the monastery of Saint George Krimnon on Zakynthos. No hymn is printed. Akakios of Kausokalyvia, whose life he imitated and whom the page keeps on 12 Απριλίου, has no folder, so he is named without a link.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 03.06.2026 (21. мај ст. ст.) — „Преподобни мученик Пахомије.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, on the same menologion 21/5 the Greek row already carries, and the same man: beheaded at Uşak in 1730 on the Ascension, his relics at Patmos. **A DAY OF DEATH THAT DIFFERS FROM HIS FEAST BY EXACTLY THIRTEEN DAYS, AND THERE IS NO FIELD FOR IT.** „најзад посеку 8. маја 1730. године, на сам дан Вазнесења“ — **8 May**, where every calendar that keeps him, this book included, keeps him on **21 May**. **21 less 8 is thirteen**, which BRIEF.md §8 names as the signature of the style conversion — but that rule is about two **feast** dates, and this is a date of death against a feast, so **it is recorded and not resolved**: the row is the 21 May this book prints as its day, no day is moved, and the 8 May stands in the prose and in this note. **saint.gr agrees on the Ascension and gives no day-number at all**, «μαρτύρησε δι' αποκεφαλισμού το 1730 μ.Χ., την Πέμπτη της Αναλήψεως», so the two books agree on the year and on the feast and only this one gives the day. **It is the fifth day of death this wave has had to put in prose**, after Cyril’s 14 February, Methodius’s 6 April, Isidore of Rostov’s 14 May and Stephen of Piperi’s 20 May. **`dates` untouched**: `death` 1730 is already there off saint.gr and this book gives the same year. **New here, and it is almost the whole of a life saint.gr gives in one sentence**: that he was **„Родом из Мале Русије“**, of Little Russia, and a „сељак малоруски“, a Little-Russian peasant; that **the Tatars caught him in his youth and sold him to a Turkish tanner as a slave**; that he **spent twenty-seven years in slavery at Uşaki in Asia Minor** and was **made a Turk by force**; that he went to the Holy Mountain, was tonsured and **spent twelve years at the monastery of Saint Paul**; that **his elder and spiritual father Јосиф went with him back to Uşaki**, where **he showed himself to his former master as a Christian in monastic dress**; that he was tortured, thrown into prison and beheaded; and that **many wonders came of his blood and his relics**. **The two durations are not dates**: twenty-seven years of slavery and twelve on Athos, with a death in 1730, invite a birth and none is reckoned — the seventh such refusal in seven days. **His elder Joseph gains no folder and no row**: the entry gives him nothing but a name and an office, no calendar read for this corpus can be shown to keep him, and by the coordinator’s third ruling nothing is minted for him. `types` untouched — Преподобни мученик is exactly the `venerable-martyr` this folder carries, and the `new-martyr` and `monk` stand uncontradicted. **`related` untouched**: `john-the-theologian` is already its one row and is there because of the church on Patmos, which this entry confirms. No `locations`, although Little Russia, Uşaki, the Holy Mountain and Patmos are all named. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
